evals.prompt: ok so i added a method to one of our port traits and now `cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` blows up with error[E0277]: the trait bound `fn(Extension<Arc<dyn Port>>) -> _ {handler}: Handler<_, _>` is not satisfied. native build is fine. i read workers-rs futures aren't Send so i switched the trait to #[async_trait(?Send)] on wasm only with a cfg_attr and now it's still broken (and the router in thrust-api is shared with the server). what do i do
evals.expected_output: Explains that axum's Router needs Send handler futures on every target it is compiled for, so a cfg switch cannot work; keep the port trait plain #[async_trait] on all targets; wrap only the JS-touching blocks in worker::send::SendFuture inside the Cloudflare adapters crate; do not put #[worker::send] in the shared api crate; run scripts/check-deps.sh and the wasm32 cargo check.
expectations: States that axum handler futures must be Send on every target the shared router is compiled for, including wasm32.
Tells the user to declare the port trait with plain #[async_trait] on all targets, removing both the ?Send and the cfg_attr switch.
Tells the user to wrap JS-backed futures in worker::send::SendFuture (or SendFuture::new(async move { .. })) inside the Cloudflare adapters crate, not in core or ports.
Does not recommend adding a worker dependency to the shared router crate (thrust-api) or to ports/core.
Mentions running scripts/check-deps.sh (or otherwise re-checking the dependency graph) after the change.

evals.prompt: wasm bundle was 2.1MB so i set strip = true in [profile.release] and added panic = "abort" at the workspace level to shave more. worker-build now dies with 'externref table required for catch wrappers' and separately our native thrust-server stopped returning 500 JSON on handler panics, the whole process just dies. help
evals.expected_output: Revert strip to "debuginfo" (strip = true drops the wasm target_features section so wasm-bindgen does not enable externref); remove the panic key (wasm32-unknown-unknown is already panic=abort; the native server must keep unwinding for CatchPanicLayer).
expectations: Tells the user to change strip = true back to strip = "debuginfo".
Explains that strip = true drops the wasm target_features section so wasm-bindgen does not enable externref, producing the 'externref table required for catch wrappers' error.
Tells the user to remove the workspace-wide panic = "abort" setting.
Explains that wasm32-unknown-unknown already aborts on panic, so the key is unnecessary for the Worker.
Explains that the native server needs unwinding for CatchPanicLayer to catch handler panics and return the 500 response.

evals.prompt: on my mac `cargo build --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` says can't find crate for `std` even though i already ran rustup target add. i put the rustup bin dir first on PATH and now linking dies with dyld: Library not loaded: @rpath/libLLVM.dylib. i've got homebrew rust installed too. what is going on and what's the repo way to run this
evals.expected_output: Homebrew rustc shadows rustup's and has no wasm32 std; rustup target add is not the fix because the target is already under rustup. The second error is rust-lld missing libLLVM on its rpath. Both are handled by running through scripts/rs.
expectations: Identifies that the cargo/rustc on PATH is Homebrew's, whose sysroot has no wasm32-unknown-unknown standard library, as the cause of the 'can't find crate for std' error.
States that re-running rustup target add is not the fix because the wasm32 target is already installed under the rustup toolchain.
Identifies the dyld error as rustup's rust-lld not finding libLLVM.dylib, which lives in the toolchain lib directory.
Tells the user to run the command through scripts/rs (for example scripts/rs cargo check --target wasm32-unknown-unknown).
Mentions that the wrapper sets DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH inside itself rather than relying on a variable exported in the user's shell.

evals.prompt: wrangler dev (4.123.0) for the rust worker fails: 'This Worker requires compatibility date "2026-10-01", but the newest date supported by this server binary is "2026-08-18"'. i bumped compatibility_date to today to get a new flag. do i need to upgrade wrangler or is something else off?
evals.expected_output: VERSION-PINNED: 2026-08-18 is the limit of the workerd bundled with wrangler 4.123.0; a different wrangler has a different limit, so expectations 2 and 3 follow the date in the error text. The local workerd bundled with wrangler caps the compatibility date; set compatibility_date at or below the date in the error message in the wrangler config(s); do not rely on workerd --version; re-measure after upgrading wrangler.
expectations: Explains that the workerd bundled with the local wrangler limits the maximum compatibility_date, and the error message states that maximum.
Tells the user to set compatibility_date to a date no later than the one quoted in the error (2026-08-18).
Says to check both wrangler config files in the Worker crate (wrangler.toml and wrangler.memory.toml).
Does not claim that the output of workerd --version is the accepted maximum date.
Says that after upgrading wrangler the limit should be re-measured by trying a date rather than assumed.

evals.prompt: we need a Cloudflare Workflow kicked off from our rust worker (after an outbox sweep). can i just write the WorkflowEntrypoint in rust with workers-rs? what's the pattern we already use here
evals.expected_output: workers-rs 0.8.7 cannot define a Workflow class; use the JS shim entry.mjs that re-exports the Rust Worker and adds the class; Rust triggers it via env.WORKFLOW.create through js_sys::Reflect; shim holds no business logic and calls back into Rust through a service binding; refer to Cloudflare docs for Workflow semantics.
expectations: States that workers-rs 0.8.7 provides no way to define a Workflow class from Rust, and that a Rust-exported class via wasm-bindgen is untested.
Points to the JS shim crates/thrust-worker/entry.mjs, which re-exports the Rust Worker and defines the Workflow class.
Says Rust triggers the Workflow by calling the binding's create method through js_sys::Reflect / wasm-bindgen.
Says the shim must contain no business logic and calls back into the Rust Worker through the SELF service binding.
Points to Cloudflare's own Workflows documentation for step semantics instead of restating them.
